findings.description: At 0:00 the bowl holds 8 fully visible balls: 2 red, 3 green, 3 yellow. At 0:00.75-0:01.0 the child lifts a red ball out of the bowl, but the bowl still shows the same 8 balls, both reds included, in their original places. That makes 9 balls and 3 reds. Nothing was added from outside the bowl, so the extra red ball has no visible source. It is effectively a duplicate.

Before the stirring there were about 3 red, 3 green and 3 yellow balls. In the final frames (0:09.25-0:09.75) about 4-5 distinct red balls are visible, only 1-2 green and 1 yellow. Stirring cannot add red balls or remove yellow ones (no balls leave the bowl), so balls seem to change color or identity during the mix.

From 0:09.0 to 0:09.75 the rigid round balls look lumpy and squashed, even blocky (e.g. the green ball at the bottom centre at 0:09.75). Motion blur alone does not explain this. The balls were clean spheres earlier, and nothing visible deforms them.
